title: Resolve top-two Crew votes using the canonical deterministic tie policy
prompt: Read README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/SWARM_PILOT.md, docs/PILOT100_BACKLOG.md and the frozen sources under docs/design/ first. RULES-SPEC-v1.md is the canonical six-node deterministic gameplay contract; completed foundation APIs remain compatibility history. Implement new versioned APIs without changing the completed T01–T10 contracts. Work only in declared ownership; no manifests, shared exports or dependencies unless explicitly owned. Engine production remains ES2022-only, pure and independent from Firebase, Node, browser, UI and Capacitor. Use original synthetic test data and injected authority time/entropy; no clocks or global randomness in engine. Never expose seed, roles, private inputs or raw audit data through public output. Do not invent a rule where an explicit design gap is named. Run scoped lint/typecheck/tests and npm run check; report contract changes and observed results. No commits, pushes, PRs, child agents, cloud deployment, credentials or budget changes. Count single-target votes and select the two highest totals. At either tied seat, prioritize the tied eligible candidate with the longest time since Crew service, then a server-seeded visible draw if still tied; stable seat order defines input ordering so map iteration cannot affect a draw. Lead never breaks ties. Record an allowlisted public draw explanation without the seed/RNG or roles. Preserve the one-round cooldown constraint. D-ELIGIBLE-POOL must define continuation when legal candidates fall below two; never silently waive a restriction to manufacture a Crew.
acceptance: First-seat and second-seat ties obey vote total, longest-since-Crew and seeded draw in that exact order.
Identical vote/history/RNG inputs produce the same two distinct eligible members and exact RNG advancement.
Public draw events explain the actual candidate tie/winner without exposing private role or future random state.
Scoped lint, typecheck and tests plus npm run check pass; legacy APIs retain compatibility and only owned files change.
